subject: Physics
subtopic: Uniform Rectilinear Motion, Constant Acceleration & Free Fall under Gravity
text: MoEYS Grade 10 Physics Chapter 1: 1D Rectilinear Kinematics (ស៊ីនេម៉ាទិចនៃចលនាត្រង់) and Free Fall (ទំនាក់សេរី). Covers reference frames, displacement vs distance, uniform rectilinear motion x = x_0 + vt, uniformly varied rectilinear motion (v = v_0 + at, x = x_0 + v_0 t + (1/2)at^2, v^2 - v_0^2 = 2ad), and vertical free fall under gravity g.

source.section: Uniform Rectilinear Motion, Constant Acceleration & Free Fall under Gravity

metadata.topic_khmer: ចលនាត្រង់ និងទំនាក់សេរី
metadata.subtopic_khmer: ចលនាត្រង់ស្មើ ចលនាត្រង់ប្រែប្រួលស្មើ និងទំនាក់សេរី
metadata.khmer_description: សិក្សាចលនាត្រង់ស្មើ ចលនាត្រង់ប្រែប្រួលស្មើ សមីការល្បឿននិងទីតាំង និងចលនាទំនាក់សេរីក្រោមសំទុះទំនាញផែនដី g។
metadata.starter_problem: v_0 = 20\text{ m/s}, \; v = 0, \; d = 50\text{ m}, \quad \text{find acceleration } a \text{ and braking time } t
learning_objectives: Convert speeds between km/h and m/s and distinguish displacement from distance
Solve constant-acceleration problems using kinematic equations
Calculate fall time, height, and impact velocity in vertical free fall

concepts.title: Uniformly Varied Rectilinear Motion & Free Fall (ចលនាត្រង់ប្រែប្រួលស្មើ និងទំនាក់សេរី)
concepts.summary: v = v_0 + at, d = v_0 t + (1/2)at^2, v^2 - v_0^2 = 2ad, and free fall h = (1/2)gt^2.
concepts.body: When acceleration a is constant along a straight line, velocity changes linearly with time (v = v_0 + at) and displacement is quadratic in time. Free fall from rest is uniformly accelerated vertical motion with a = g approx 9.8 m/s^2, giving h = (1/2)gt^2 and v = sqrt(2gh).

khmer_terms.1D Kinematics & Free Fall: ចលនាត្រង់ និងទំនាក់សេរី
khmer_terms.Uniform Rectilinear Motion, Constant Acc: ចលនាត្រង់ស្មើ ចលនាត្រង់ប្រែប្រួលស្មើ និងទំនាក់សេរី
khmer_terms.uniform rectilinear motion: ចលនាត្រង់ស្មើ
khmer_terms.uniformly varied motion: ចលនាត្រង់ប្រែប្រួលស្មើ
khmer_terms.free fall: ទំនាក់សេរី

formulas.name: 1D Constant-Acceleration & Free-Fall Equations
formulas.expression: v = v_0 + at, \quad d = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2}at^2, \quad v^2 - v_0^2 = 2ad, \quad h = \frac{1}{2}gt^2

examples.problem: A car traveling at 72 km/h brakes uniformly to a complete stop over a distance of 50 m. Find its acceleration a and braking time t.
solution_steps: Step 1: Convert v_0 = 72 / 3.6 = 20 m/s, final velocity v = 0.
Step 3: Find time: t = (v - v_0)/a = (0 - 20)/(-4) = 5 s.

exercises.prompt: A stone is dropped from rest from a bridge and hits the water after 3 s (take g = 9.8 m/s^2). Find the height of the bridge and impact speed.

solution_steps: Step 1: Convert all quantities to SI units (divide km/h by 3.6 to get m/s).
Step 2: Choose the kinematic equation that connects the knowns and target unknown.
Step 3: Solve and check the sign of velocity and acceleration.

common_misconceptions.text: Substituting v_0 in km/h directly into v^2 - v_0^2 = 2ad without converting to m/s.
common_misconceptions.correction: Always divide km/h by 3.6 to obtain m/s before using SI acceleration in m/s^2.

Introduce core concept and governing formulas
Walk through step-by-step worked examples on the whiteboard
Check student understanding with guided exercises and misconception checks

subject: Physics
subtopic: Newton's Three Laws, Weight, Spring Elasticity & Sliding Friction
text: MoEYS Grade 10 Physics Chapter 2: Dynamics (ឌីណាមិច) and Mechanical Forces (កម្លាំងមេកានិច). Covers inertia, Newton's First, Second (sum F = ma), and Third Laws (F_{AB} = -F_{BA}), weight P = mg, Hooke's law for elastic springs F_e = k Delta l, and static and kinetic friction f_k = mu_k N.

source.section: Newton's Three Laws, Weight, Spring Elasticity & Sliding Friction

metadata.topic_khmer: ច្បាប់ញូតុន កម្លាំងកកិត និងច្បាប់ហ៊ុក
metadata.subtopic_khmer: ច្បាប់ទាំងបីរបស់ញូតុន ទម្ងន់ កម្លាំងយឺតនៃរ៉ឺស័រ និងកម្លាំងកកិត
metadata.khmer_description: សិក្សាច្បាប់ទាំងបីរបស់ញូតុន ទម្ងន់និងម៉ាស ច្បាប់ហ៊ុកសម្រាប់រ៉ឺស័រ និងកម្លាំងកកិតលើប្លង់ដេកនិងប្លង់ទេរ។
metadata.starter_problem: m = 5\text{ kg}, \; F = 25\text{ N}, \; \mu_k = 0.2, \; g = 10\text{ m/s}^2, \quad \text{find acceleration } a
learning_objectives: Draw free-body diagrams and apply Newton's second law sum F = ma
Compute spring stiffness or elongation using Hooke's law F_e = k Delta l
Calculate normal force N and kinetic friction f_k = mu_k N

concepts.title: Newton's Second Law, Hooke's Law & Friction (ច្បាប់ទី២ញូតុន ច្បាប់ហ៊ុក និងកម្លាំងកកិត)
concepts.summary: sum F = ma, spring force F_e = k Delta l, and sliding friction f_k = mu_k N.
concepts.body: The vector sum of forces on a body equals mass times acceleration: sum F = ma. Within the elastic limit, a spring of stiffness k stretched by Delta l exerts restoring force F_e = k Delta l. A sliding surface exerts kinetic friction f_k = mu_k N opposing relative motion.

khmer_terms.Newton's Laws, Friction & Hooke's Law: ច្បាប់ញូតុន កម្លាំងកកិត និងច្បាប់ហ៊ុក
khmer_terms.Newton's Three Laws, Weight, Spring Elas: ច្បាប់ទាំងបីរបស់ញូតុន ទម្ងន់ កម្លាំងយឺតនៃរ៉ឺស័រ និងកម្លាំងកកិត
khmer_terms.Newton's second law: ច្បាប់ទី២ញូតុន
khmer_terms.Hooke's law: ច្បាប់ហ៊ុក
khmer_terms.spring constant: កម្រាញ់រ៉ឺស័រ k
khmer_terms.kinetic friction: កម្លាំងកកិតរអិល f_k

formulas.name: Newton's Second Law, Hooke's Law & Kinetic Friction
formulas.expression: \sum \vec{F} = m\vec{a}, \quad F_e = k\Delta l, \quad f_k = \mu_k N

examples.problem: A 5 kg block on a horizontal floor (mu_k = 0.2, g = 10 m/s^2) is pulled horizontally by a force F = 25 N. Find its acceleration.
solution_steps: Step 1: Vertical equilibrium gives N = mg = 5 * 10 = 50 N.
Step 2: Kinetic friction f_k = mu_k N = 0.2 * 50 = 10 N.
Step 3: Horizontal Newton's second law: a = (F - f_k)/m = (25 - 10)/5 = 3 m/s^2.

exercises.prompt: A spring of stiffness k = 200 N/m hangs vertically supporting a 3 kg mass in equilibrium (g = 10 m/s^2). Find its extension Delta l in cm.

solution_steps: Step 1: Draw a free-body diagram showing weight, normal force, applied force, and friction/spring force.
Step 2: Project forces onto perpendicular axes to find N and f_k.
Step 3: Solve sum F_x = m a_x for acceleration.

common_misconceptions.text: Confusing mass m (in kg) with weight P = mg (in N).
common_misconceptions.correction: Mass is an intrinsic scalar property in kg, whereas weight is the gravitational force mg in Newtons.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Mechanical Work, Power, Efficiency, Levers, Pulleys & Inclined Planes
text: MoEYS Grade 10 Physics Chapter 3: Mechanical Work (កម្មន្ត), Power (អានុភាព), and Simple Machines (ម៉ាស៊ីនងាយ). Covers work W = Fd cos(theta), motor work vs resistive work, mechanical power P = W/t = Fv, levers, fixed and movable pulleys, inclined planes, the Golden Rule of Mechanics, and efficiency eta = (W_u / W_t) * 100%.

source.section: Mechanical Work, Power, Efficiency, Levers, Pulleys & Inclined Planes

metadata.topic_khmer: កម្មន្ត អានុភាព និងម៉ាស៊ីនងាយ
metadata.subtopic_khmer: កម្មន្តមេកានិច អានុភាព ទិន្នផល ឃ្នាស់ រ៉ក និងប្លង់ទេរ
metadata.khmer_description: សិក្សាកម្មន្តមេកានិច អានុភាព ម៉ាស៊ីនងាយ (ឃ្នាស់ រ៉ក ប្លង់ទេរ) វិធានមាសនៃមេកានិច និងទិន្នផលមេកានិច។
metadata.starter_problem: m = 60\text{ kg}, \; h = 2\text{ m}, \; l = 5\text{ m}, \; F = 300\text{ N}, \quad \text{find efficiency } \eta
learning_objectives: Calculate mechanical work W = Fd cos(theta) and power P = W/t = Fv
Analyze force-distance trade-offs in levers, pulleys, and inclined planes
Compute useful work, total work, and mechanical efficiency eta

concepts.title: Work, Power & Efficiency of Simple Machines (កម្មន្ត អានុភាព និងទិន្នផលម៉ាស៊ីនងាយ)
concepts.summary: W = Fd cos(theta), P = W/t = Fv, and efficiency eta = (W_useful / W_total) * 100%.
concepts.body: A constant force F acting over displacement d at angle theta performs work W = Fd cos(theta). Power is P = W/t = Fv. Simple machines reduce required effort force by increasing displacement; in real machines with friction, efficiency is eta = (W_u / W_t) * 100% < 100%.

khmer_terms.Work, Power & Simple Machines: កម្មន្ត អានុភាព និងម៉ាស៊ីនងាយ
khmer_terms.Mechanical Work, Power, Efficiency, Leve: កម្មន្តមេកានិច អានុភាព ទិន្នផល ឃ្នាស់ រ៉ក និងប្លង់ទេរ
khmer_terms.mechanical work: កម្មន្តមេកានិច W
khmer_terms.simple machine: ម៉ាស៊ីនងាយ
khmer_terms.mechanical efficiency: ទិន្នផលមេកានិច eta

examples.problem: A worker pulls a 60 kg crate up a 5 m inclined plane to a vertical height of 2 m using a force F = 300 N parallel to the incline (g = 10 m/s^2). Find useful work, total work, and efficiency eta.
solution_steps: Step 1: Useful work W_u = mgh = 60 * 10 * 2 = 1200 J.
Step 2: Total work W_t = F * l = 300 * 5 = 1500 J.
Step 3: Efficiency eta = (1200 / 1500) * 100% = 80%.

exercises.prompt: A crane lifts a 400 kg load vertically at a constant speed of 1.5 m/s (g = 10 m/s^2). What power does the crane deliver?
hints: Use P = Fv with F = mg.

solution_steps: Step 1: Identify the useful load work W_u = mgh and total input work W_t = Fl.
Step 2: Compute power P = W/t or P = Fv.
Step 3: Evaluate efficiency eta = (W_u / W_t) * 100%.

common_misconceptions.text: Believing a simple machine reduces total work required.
common_misconceptions.correction: By the Golden Rule of Mechanics, reducing force by a factor k requires pulling through k times the distance, so work is never saved.

Walk through step-by-step worked examples on the whiteboard

subject: Physics
subtopic: Hydrostatic Pressure, Pascal's Law, Hydraulic Press & Archimedes' Buoyancy
text: MoEYS Grade 10 Physics Chapter 4: Fluid Statics (ស្តាទិចនៃសន្ទនីយ៍), Hydrostatic Pressure, and Buoyancy. Covers pressure p = F/S, absolute hydrostatic pressure at depth h (p = p_0 + rho g h), Pascal's law and hydraulic lifts (F_1/S_1 = F_2/S_2), and Archimedes' buoyant force F_A = rho_fluid g V_sub.

source.section: Hydrostatic Pressure, Pascal's Law, Hydraulic Press & Archimedes' Buoyancy

metadata.topic_khmer: ស្តាទិចនៃសន្ទនីយ៍ សម្ពាធ និងដំណោលអាកស៊ីម៉ែត
metadata.subtopic_khmer: សម្ពាធអ៊ីដ្រូស្តាទិច ច្បាប់ប៉ាស្កាល់ ឃ្នាស់អ៊ីដ្រូលិច និងដំណោលអាកស៊ីម៉ែត
metadata.khmer_description: សិក្សាសម្ពាធអ៊ីដ្រូស្តាទិច ច្បាប់ប៉ាស្កាល់និងឃ្នាស់អ៊ីដ្រូលិច ព្រមទាំងដំណោលអាកស៊ីម៉ែតនិងលក្ខខណ្ឌអណ្ដែតនៃអង្គធាតុ។
metadata.starter_problem: S_1 = 20\text{ cm}^2, \; S_2 = 500\text{ cm}^2, \; F_2 = 15000\text{ N}, \quad \text{find hydraulic force } F_1
learning_objectives: Compute hydrostatic pressure p = p_0 + rho g h at depth h in a liquid
Apply Pascal's principle F_1/S_1 = F_2/S_2 to hydraulic presses
Calculate Archimedes' buoyant force F_A = rho_fluid g V_sub and determine floating conditions

concepts.title: Pascal's Law & Archimedes' Buoyant Force (ច្បាប់ប៉ាស្កាល់ និងដំណោលអាកស៊ីម៉ែត)
concepts.summary: F_1/S_1 = F_2/S_2 in hydraulic systems; upward buoyant force is F_A = rho_fluid g V_sub.
concepts.body: External pressure applied to a confined liquid is transmitted equally in all directions (F_1/S_1 = F_2/S_2). Any object partially or wholly immersed in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the displaced fluid: F_A = rho_fluid g V_sub.

khmer_terms.Hydrostatics, Pressure & Archimedes' Pri: ស្តាទិចនៃសន្ទនីយ៍ សម្ពាធ និងដំណោលអាកស៊ីម៉ែត
khmer_terms.Hydrostatic Pressure, Pascal's Law, Hydr: សម្ពាធអ៊ីដ្រូស្តាទិច ច្បាប់ប៉ាស្កាល់ ឃ្នាស់អ៊ីដ្រូលិច និងដំណោលអាកស៊ីម៉ែត
khmer_terms.hydrostatic pressure: សម្ពាធអ៊ីដ្រូស្តាទិច
khmer_terms.Pascal's law: ច្បាប់ប៉ាស្កាល់
khmer_terms.hydraulic press: ឃ្នាស់អ៊ីដ្រូលិច
khmer_terms.Archimedes' buoyant force: ដំណោលអាកស៊ីម៉ែត F_A

formulas.name: Hydrostatic Pressure, Hydraulic Press & Archimedes' Law
formulas.expression: p = p_0 + \rho g h, \quad \frac{F_1}{S_1} = \frac{F_2}{S_2}, \quad F_A = \rho_{\text{fluid}} g V_{\text{sub}}

examples.problem: A hydraulic lift has piston areas S_1 = 20 cm^2 and S_2 = 500 cm^2. What force F_1 on the small piston supports a 1500 kg car on the large piston (g = 10 m/s^2)?
solution_steps: Step 1: Weight on large piston F_2 = mg = 1500 * 10 = 15000 N.

exercises.prompt: A solid block of volume V = 0.002 m^3 is completely submerged in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 10 m/s^2). Calculate the buoyant force F_A.

solution_steps: Step 1: Identify fluid density rho_fluid, submerged volume V_sub, or piston areas S_1, S_2.
Step 2: Apply p = p_0 + rho g h, F_1/S_1 = F_2/S_2, or F_A = rho_fluid g V_sub.
Step 3: Check units (Pa, N, m^3).

common_misconceptions.text: Using the density of the solid body instead of the fluid density in F_A = rho g V_sub.
common_misconceptions.correction: Archimedes' force equals the weight of the displaced FLUID, so always use rho_fluid.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Temperature Scales, Linear/Volume Expansion, Specific Heat & Latent Heat
text: MoEYS Grade 10 Physics Chapters 5–6: Thermometry, Thermal Expansion (ការរីកកម្ដៅ), and Calorimetry (កាឡូរីមាត្រ). Covers Kelvin and Celsius scales T(K) = t(C) + 273, linear thermal expansion Delta l = alpha l_0 Delta T, volumetric expansion Delta V = beta V_0 Delta T (beta approx 3 alpha), sensible heat Q = mc Delta T, latent heat Q = mL, and heat balance sum Q = 0.

source.section: Temperature Scales, Linear/Volume Expansion, Specific Heat & Latent Heat

metadata.topic_khmer: សីតុណ្ហភាព ការរីកកម្ដៅ និងកាឡូរីមាត្រ
metadata.subtopic_khmer: មាត្រដ្ឋានសីតុណ្ហភាព ការរីកកម្ដៅ បរិមាណកម្ដៅ និងកម្ដៅឡាតង់
metadata.khmer_description: សិក្សាមាត្រដ្ឋានសីតុណ្ហភាព ការរីកបណ្ដោយនិងរីកមាឌនៃអង្គធាតុរឹងនិងរាវ បរិមាណកម្ដៅ Q = mc Delta T កម្ដៅឡាតង់ Q = mL និងសមីការតុល្យភាពកម្ដៅ។
metadata.starter_problem: m = 0.5\text{ kg ice at } 0^\circ\text{C} \to \text{water at } 20^\circ\text{C}, \quad \text{find total heat } Q
learning_objectives: Convert between Celsius, Kelvin, and Fahrenheit scales and compute thermal expansion
Calculate heat transfer during temperature changes (Q = mc Delta T) and phase transitions (Q = mL)
Solve thermal equilibrium problems using sum Q_i = 0

concepts.title: Thermal Expansion, Sensible Heat & Latent Heat (ការរីកកម្ដៅ បរិមាណកម្ដៅ និងកម្ដៅឡាតង់)
concepts.summary: Delta l = alpha l_0 Delta T, Q = mc Delta T for temperature change, and Q = mL for phase change.
concepts.body: Heating a rod of length l_0 by Delta T increases its length by Delta l = alpha l_0 Delta T. Warming mass m without phase change requires Q = mc Delta T, whereas melting or vaporizing at constant temperature requires Q = mL. In an isolated calorimeter, sum Q_gained + sum Q_lost = 0.

khmer_terms.Temperature, Thermal Expansion & Calorim: សីតុណ្ហភាព ការរីកកម្ដៅ និងកាឡូរីមាត្រ
khmer_terms.Temperature Scales, Linear/Volume Expans: មាត្រដ្ឋានសីតុណ្ហភាព ការរីកកម្ដៅ បរិមាណកម្ដៅ និងកម្ដៅឡាតង់
khmer_terms.linear thermal expansion: ការរីកបណ្ដោយ
khmer_terms.specific heat capacity: កម្ដៅម៉ាស c
khmer_terms.latent heat: កម្ដៅឡាតង់ L
khmer_terms.thermal equilibrium: លំនឹងកម្ដៅ

formulas.name: Linear Expansion, Sensible Heat & Latent Heat
formulas.expression: \Delta l = \alpha l_0 \Delta T, \quad Q = mc(T_f - T_i), \quad Q_{\text{phase}} = mL, \quad \sum Q_i = 0

examples.problem: How much heat is needed to turn 0.5 kg of ice at 0 deg C into liquid water at 20 deg C? (L_f = 3.34e5 J/kg, c_w = 4180 J/(kg*K))
solution_steps: Step 1: Heat to melt ice at 0 deg C: Q_1 = m L_f = 0.5 * 3.34e5 = 167000 J.
Step 2: Heat to warm water from 0 deg C to 20 deg C: Q_2 = m c_w Delta T = 0.5 * 4180 * 20 = 41800 J.
Step 3: Total heat Q = Q_1 + Q_2 = 208800 J = 208.8 kJ.

exercises.prompt: A steel rail has length l_0 = 25 m at 20 deg C (alpha = 1.2e-5 K^-1). By how many millimeters does it expand at 45 deg C?

solution_steps: Step 1: Check if any substance undergoes a phase change (melting or boiling).
Step 2: Write Q = mc Delta T for each temperature change and Q = mL for each phase transition.
Step 3: Sum heat terms or solve sum Q_i = 0 for the equilibrium temperature.

common_misconceptions.text: Forgetting to include the latent heat of fusion m L_f when ice at 0 deg C melts into water.
common_misconceptions.correction: Ice at 0 deg C must first absorb Q_1 = m L_f to become liquid water at 0 deg C before its temperature can rise.

teaching_sequence: Review prerequisites and Khmer MoEYS terminology
Introduce core concept and governing formulas
Walk through step-by-step worked examples on the whiteboard
Check student understanding with guided exercises and misconception checks
